comments.author: Joe Oakhart
comments.body:
PASS-4 COACH + UNIFIED-SCORE + ADVISORY-CAP work on the plan-review gate (epic 5fd2). Summary of the arc.

== 1. Pass-4 affirmative COACH (added to 5fd2 + new child 75a9 crusty-herb-stand) ==
A single-turn, structured-output LLM call (NOT an agent) running after Pass-3 over the surviving advisory findings,
priming the caller with a productive NEXT MOVE per finding (beyond returning findings). Maps each finding to a move
from a fixed, project-extensible MOVE REGISTRY (moves 1-9 + 11 propagate-revisions-to-children + 12 generalize-the-
finding; move 10 reference-class cut) and emits {move_id, subject, finding_refs}; coaching prose rendered
DETERMINISTICALLY from each move's LOCKED template (LLM authors no free prose). Design A/B/D approved; C re-derived
for LLM RECIPIENTS (human-pedagogy dropped after research — LLMs can't self-correct from reflection (Huang/DeepMind),
sycophancy makes them over-adopt confident wrong fixes, lost-in-the-middle): C1 actionable-guidance-not-executable;
C2 reference findings by id (no restate); C3 select-from-registry + fill-subject; C4 cap/cluster/front-load. The
coach is a single-turn structured-output call by design (no tooling).

== 2. Self-review of the coach (log plum-strut-reek/jibe-ditty-ant) found + fixed 3 real ones ==
- ADVISORY: C1 was NOT enforced "by construction" — `subject` is a free-text field the template interpolates, so a
  solution could be smuggled in. FIX: a SUBJECT VALIDATOR (bounded noun-phrase; code/imperative/solution rejected).
- finding-`id` was minted by no child (75a9<->db7b circular). FIX: the orchestrator ca03 MINTS it (sole owner);
  db7b + 75a9 CONSUME it. (Exactly the move-#11 propagation gap the coach exists to coach.)
- the "Review structure — three-pass" section omitted Pass-4. FIX: added it.
Also filed bug `slim-fetch-ledge` (ed2b): `rebar show` intermittently returns empty stdout under concurrent
background auto-push (REBAR_SYNC_PUSH=always); confirmed by it working reliably with push=off.

== 3. Unified priority SCORE (design decision) ==
Validity and impact are BOTH LLM-judged spectrums (neither absolute): a low-validity/high-impact finding may warrant
surfacing (confirm it's not real); a high-validity/low-impact one may not need a remedy to ship. So they are COMBINED
into ONE deterministic priority score (NOT two separate gates), used for both the block threshold and the advisory
ranking. (Supersedes an earlier split-axis proposal.)

== 4. Cap-dilution EXPERIMENT (workflow; advisory-cap-dilution v1 -> v2) ==
Tested H1 = "as the non-blocking list grows, an LLM reviser ignores the high-value findings". v1 hit a CEILING
(seeded defects too easy; no-findings floor 0.81; all list-sizes = 1.0 — useless). v2 (finding-dependent HARD defects
= TOCTOU/lost-update/unsafe-default/missing-failure-path; STRICT grader; L up to 32; null-safe agg):
  floor (no findings) = 0.41  ->  high-value remediation: L4=0.99, L12=0.96, L20=0.98, L32=0.91.
=> findings clearly MATTER (floor 0.41 -> ~0.99 surfaced), but NO material LLM dilution of high-value action up to
~20 (only a slight, noisy dip at 32). Refutes the strong "large list -> ignore all" claim FOR A STRONG SINGLE-PASS
REVISER IN THIS RANGE; consistent with the literature (Greptile 19% was HUMANS; IFScale collapse is at hundreds of
items). The model triages substantive findings, and "addressing" a flagged PLAN issue is cheap.
LIMITATIONS (valuable but INCONCLUSIVE ALONE): only one (strong) model — did NOT test a smaller model (Sonnet); did
NOT run under CONTEXT PRESSURE (a common cause of agents shortcutting / ignoring feedback); 1 model x 2 plans x R=6.
Artifacts: workflow scripts advisory-cap-dilution(-v2) in the session workflows dir (not committed).

== 5. DECISION + REVISIONS APPLIED (this turn; epic + children, all gate-pass) ==
- CAP = 10, CONFIG-DRIVEN (owned by 55de), TUNED later from real-world dogfood data — not a validated constant.
- The cap = top-N ADVISORY by the unified score; advisory overflow -> REVIEW_RESULT sidecar (not surfaced). Volume
  (the cap), not labeling, is the lever that preserves LLM action (research-grounded).
- THE CAP NEVER DROPS BLOCKING FINDINGS: blocking is EXEMPT; if blocking count > cap, ALL blocking findings are
  returned. The cap can never weaken a block.
- ITERATION-FATIGUE rationale encoded: LLMs frustrated across review rounds (round 3/4 keeps surfacing NEW findings)
  tend to FORCE PAST a blocked gate rather than keep addressing feedback; a bounded prioritized convergent advisory
  surface + never-drop-blocking mitigate this.
- Tickets revised: 5fd2 (cap + unified score + iteration-fatigue + experiment & limitations), 487d Pass-3 aggregator
  (unified score + cap mechanics + blocking-exempt), 55de config schema (+= advisory cap), 75a9 coach (input = the
  capped advisory set; blocking surfaced uncapped).

NEXT (not now): tune the cap from dogfood data; the deferred experiment arms (smaller model + context pressure) would
firm up the dilution picture; implement per the children when work begins (registry/orchestrator first).

comments.body:
PASS 1 review (A1 — anti-slop / over-engineering / NIH). One finding (NIH / rebuilds-existing-artifact) plus affirmations.

AFFIRMATIONS (A1 sub-checks that PASS):
- YAGNI: the doc serves a CURRENT done-definition — the plan-review epic 5fd2's "Docs" AC and its "reuse rebar.llm extension points" / "reusing the close-gate signing machinery" ACs — not a hypothetical. Affirmed.
- No new abstraction (Rule-of-Three N/A): the plan introduces NO new code abstraction, interface, or wrapper. It is documentation-only ("This is documentation only — no behavior changes") describing existing seams. Affirmed.
- No config-surface proliferation: zero new config keys proposed. Affirmed.
- No golden-hammer / cargo-cult / resume-driven / premature-optimization / premature-abstraction: no new tool/pattern/tech is forced anywhere; the AC-7 anti-drift mechanism reuses the existing introspection-test approach rather than adding redundant tooling. Affirmed.

FINDING (A1 — NIH / rebuilds an artifact already in the codebase):

- [ ] Re-scope from "create a new doc" to "audit/verify the EXISTING doc for drift", because the proposed deliverable — `docs/reuse-surface.md` — and its supporting artifacts ALREADY EXIST and already satisfy AC1–AC6; authoring it fresh would duplicate production documentation.
  - location: plan "Why" ("there is no single developer-facing API REFERENCE … This ticket creates that reference") + Acceptance Criteria line 1 ("A developer-facing API reference exists (new doc under `docs/`, e.g. `docs/reuse-surface.md` …)").
  - criteria: A1
  - evidence:
    - The plan names its own target as a hypothetical "new doc"; that exact path is present today: `docs/reuse-surface.md`, titled "Reusable machinery — developer API reference", with §1 signing / §2 LLM workflow runtime / §3 prompt library / §4 output-schema seam — the same four sections this plan enumerates.
    - AC2 already satisfied: `docs/reuse-surface.md` §1 documents `sign_manifest`/`verify_signature`/`verify_record`/`signing_key`/`key_fingerprint`/`compute_signature`/`parse_manifest`/`head_sha`, the manifest format, HMAC-SHA256/`PAYLOAD_VERSION=1` canonicalisation, the `certified|mismatch|foreign_key|unsigned` verdict table, the `head_sha` staleness binding, last-writer-wins SIGNATURE replay, AND a "Worked example — a NEW gate reusing the surface" block (lines ~103–124) — the "not just the close gate" example AC2 asks for.
    - AC3 already satisfied: §2 documents the `Runner` protocol (run/preflight), every `RunRequest` field (mode/execution_mode/output_schema/extra_tools/…), `get_runner`, PydanticAIRunner/FakeRunner, and `run_workflow(...)` with step kinds + when-to-use guidance.
    - AC4 already satisfied: §3 documents `get_prompt`/`resolve_prompt`, the closed `FRONT_MATTER_KEYS` contract, `.rebar/prompts/<id>.md` override resolution, the derived index + CI drift/parity/canonical gates, and "Adding a prompt"; §4 + `docs/output-schemas.md` document `register_contract`/`response_model_for`, `validate_structured`, packaged `src/rebar/schemas/*.schema.json`, and `OUTPUT_SCHEMAS`.
    - AC5 already satisfied: the existing doc's header states "Audience: human developers and LLM agents" and carries signatures + copy-pasteable code blocks throughout.
    - AC6 already satisfied: cross-linked at `docs/llm-framework.md:443` ("[reuse-surface.md] — the developer API reference…") and listed in `CLAUDE.md:8` ("reusable-machinery API reference `docs/reuse-surface.md`"). (Both cross-links resolve via grep today — note this contradicts earlier review comments that grepped them as absent.)
    - AC7 already satisfied: `tests/unit/test_reuse_surface_doc.py` EXISTS and is an `inspect.signature`-based anti-drift gate introspecting each documented callable (signing surface, runner/RunRequest, prompts, contracts, findings, workflow executor) — exactly the "AUTOMATED drift-check test … that introspects each documented callable" AC7 demands.
    - FP7 anti-FP (designated experiment/reference) checked and does NOT apply: the existing `docs/reuse-surface.md` is under `docs/` (not `docs/experiments/`), is not a `*_poc.*` / POC, and is already CITED BY PRODUCTION CODE (`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/registry.py:41`) and production docs (`docs/plan-review-gate.md:18,67,127`). So this is a rebuild of a production artifact, not the intended graduation of a reference/POC.
  - suggested_fix: Rewrite the "Why" to acknowledge `docs/reuse-surface.md` (+ `docs/output-schemas.md` + `tests/unit/test_reuse_surface_doc.py`) already exist, and re-scope the ticket from "create that reference" to "AUDIT the existing doc against current source for drift and fill any genuinely-missing AC item, then close." Change AC1 from "A developer-facing API reference exists (new doc…)" to "…is verified/extended". If a DIFFERENT additional doc is intended, the Why/Scope must name precisely what `docs/reuse-surface.md` is missing — as written the scope is indistinguishable from the existing file and would duplicate it.

This is the only A1 finding; the chunk is otherwise clean for this pass.

comments.author: Joe Oakhart
comments.body:
PASS-1 review (criterion T11 — data-migration / backfill safety overlay): CLEAN — no T11 findings. T11 is PASS / not-applicable for this plan.

affirmations:
- [T11] Correctly not-applicable per T11's own anti-FP rule ("not-applicable for non-persisted/in-memory changes" / "apply only when the plan changes a schema / persisted format or backfills data"). This plan's deliverables are (1) a project-level disable-the-gate config preference, (2) a written rollback/back-out runbook + deploy-ordering doc, and (3) a spec cross-reference — none of which alters an existing persisted schema or backfills/rewrites existing data, so there is no migration-EXECUTION surface (online/expand-contract, batching/throttling, resumability, dual-write window, partial-failure data-loss) for T11 to evaluate.
- [T11] The new persisted event types the plan touches (the `REVIEW_RESULT` sidecar + the `SIGNATURE`/attestation events) are ADDITIVE, append-only entries to rebar's existing event log — NOT a modification of an existing persisted schema, not a backfill/rewrite of existing rows, and not a blocking DDL on a large table. Tool-grounded: `REVIEW_RESULT` is reducer-IGNORED and compaction PRESERVES it (src/rebar/llm/plan_review/sidecar.py:7-14, src/rebar/reducer/_version.py:44); it is added like the SYNC/PRECONDITIONS precedent. No existing rows are rewritten.
- [T11] The gate DEFAULTS OFF and the cert binds to a head MATERIAL-event commit; pre-existing / in-flight tickets are simply ungated rather than backfilled, so there is deliberately no data-backfill step (the plan's own Scope frames "rollback" as turning the preference off, not migrating data).
- [T11] The genuine residual concern in this neighborhood — old+new coexistence / deploy-ordering for the new event types and mixed-version readers (Scope items 2 & 3 / AC2) — is migration-ROLLOUT/reversibility, correctly the province of T12 (rollout/rollback/reversibility), NOT T11 (migration-EXECUTION safety). Noted only to disambiguate the two overlays; it is NOT a T11 finding.

No checklist items emitted for T11.

comments.body:
PASS-1 review (T8 — LLM/prompt structural-completeness probe, overlay): CLEAN, no findings.

Applicability: T8 fires only when the plan DEFINES an LLM/agent system (new prompts, sub-agents, reviewers, output schemas, or enum vocabularies). This plan does not — it adds (1) a project-level disable-the-gate config (fail-open when off), (2) a written rollback/back-out + deploy-ordering runbook, and (3) an epic-spec cross-reference. It is a CONSUMER of the already-shipped signature/REVIEW_RESULT scheme, authoring no new prompt, decision protocol, counter, or enum.

Tool-grounded verification that every enum/schema/protocol the plan references is pre-existing and fully specified (so there is no undefined-but-referenced vocabulary):
- The signature verdict vocabulary (certified|mismatch|foreign_key|unsigned) is fully defined in src/rebar/signing.py (verify_record) and src/rebar/schemas/verify_signature_result.schema.json (enum).
- The REVIEW_RESULT sidecar is a pre-existing reducer-ignored, fsck-recognized event type (src/rebar/reducer/_version.py:44 `_NON_REPLAY_KNOWN_TYPES`; docs/plan-review-gate.md:212-221) — the plan references it for rollout/coexistence, it does not define it.
- The disable config the plan references already ships: `verify.require_plan_review_for_claim` (src/rebar/config.py:260, default off; transition.py:651,661-662).

Structural-gap checklist — all pass for this chunk:
- (a) No schema/enum referenced whose value vocabulary is never defined — verdict vocab + event types are defined in source.
- (b) No processing protocol/decision rule referenced but separated from its schema — the rollback decision rule sits with the config/event artifacts it governs; no LLM decision protocol is introduced.
- (c) No counter/state increment with ambiguous placement — none introduced (verify+transition is the existing atomic claim primitive).
- (d) No incomplete/failed sub-step lacking a fallback — the gate-off / fail-open behavior is itself the specified fallback path.
- (e) No instruction-locality / pink-elephant antipattern — no new prompt text; all referenced surfaces (signing verify, REVIEW_RESULT sidecar, claim path) exist and are fully specified (tool-verified).

Affirmations (T8): not-applicable by construction (no new LLM/agent system defined); and where enum-like terms ARE referenced, each is tool-verified to exist and be fully specified in current source. No proven structural gap — PASS.
